fullPassage: The English language has words for hundreds of emotions. Other languages have far fewer; for example, there are just seven in the Chewong language of the Malay Peninsula. As one emotion researcher put it, "Different languages recognize different emotions. They carve up the domain of emotion differently." That's not to say that different people experience different emotions, but rather that the categories of emotion identified in various cultures are somewhat arbitrary. That supports the idea that our feelings are not, as Darwin believed, innate hardwired responses to a set of archetypal stimuli. In an article co-authored with Ralph Adolphs, Barrett argued that science has not yet identified truly objective criteria to reliably determine whether a person or an animal is in one emotional state or another. Adolphs, like the majority of emotion researchers, recognizes her point, but wouldn't go that far in dismissing the usual categories. As to which school of thought is correct, the jury is still out.

❌ ④ 객관적 기준 이미 확립 — 'has not yet identified(아직 못 찾음)'라 반대예요.
det.tip: carve up the domain of emotion differently = 언어마다 감정을 다르게 나눔

ch: 모든 언어는 감정을 나타내는 단어의 수가 거의 같다.
언어에 따라 감정을 구분하고 범주화하는 방식이 다를 수 있다.
다윈의 감정 이론은 오늘날 과학적으로 완전히 입증되었다.
과학은 감정 상태를 판단할 객관적 기준을 이미 확립했다.

questions.passage: The English language has words for hundreds of emotions. Other languages have far fewer; for example, there are just seven in the Chewong language of the Malay Peninsula. As one emotion researcher put it, "Different languages recognize different emotions. They carve up the domain of emotion differently." That's not to say that different people experience different emotions, but rather that the categories of emotion identified in various cultures are somewhat arbitrary. That supports the idea that our feelings are not, as Darwin believed, innate hardwired responses to a set of archetypal stimuli. In an article co-authored with Ralph Adolphs, Barrett argued that science has not yet identified truly objective criteria to reliably determine whether a person or an animal is in one emotional state or another. Adolphs, like the majority of emotion researchers, recognizes her point, but wouldn't go that far in dismissing the usual categories. As to which school of thought is correct, the jury is still out.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: Adolphs ... recognizes her point, but wouldn't go that far ... As to which school of thought is correct, the jury is still out. 모두가 동의하는 것이 아니라 논쟁이 계속되므로 ④는 불일치.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 영어가 감정 단어 많음 — hundreds vs far fewer, 일치
✅ ② 언어마다 다르게 인식 — 'recognize different emotions', 일치
✅ ③ 객관적 기준 아직 없음 — 'has not yet identified objective criteria', 일치
❌ ④ 모든 연구자가 Barrett에 전적으로 동의 — Adolphs는 요점은 인정하되 끝까지 가지 않고, '어느 학파가 옳은지 아직 결론이 안 났다(the jury is still out)'고 했어요. '모두 전적으로 동의'는 불일치 ←정답
det.tip: the jury is still out = 아직 결론 안 남 → 모두 동의가 아님

ch: 영어는 다른 많은 언어들보다 감정 관련 단어가 많다.
한 연구자는 언어마다 감정을 다르게 인식한다고 말했다.
Barrett은 감정 상태를 판별할 객관적 기준이 아직 없다고 보았다.
모든 감정 연구자들이 Barrett의 견해에 전적으로 동의한다.

questions.passage: English has words for hundreds of emotions, ①<u>whereas</u> some other languages have far fewer. Many researchers argue that different languages ②<u>divide</u> the domain of emotion in their own ways. This idea suggests that the categories of emotion ③<u>identifying</u> in various cultures are somewhat arbitrary. Adolphs, like most emotion researchers, ④<u>recognizes</u> this point but is reluctant to abandon the usual categories.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ identifying → identified: 범주가 '확인되는' 대상이므로 수동의 과거분사 identified가 명사 categories를 뒤에서 꾸며야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ identifying — the categories of emotion identifying ...는 틀려요. 범주(categories)는 사람에 의해 '확인되는' 대상이라 수동의 과거분사 identified가 명사를 뒤에서 꾸며야 해요(categories (that are) identified). 능동의 identifying은 '범주가 무언가를 확인한다'는 뜻이 되어 어색해요 ←정답

❌ ① whereas — '~인 반면'이라는 대조 접속사로, 영어는 많고 다른 언어는 적다는 대조에 맞아요.

❌ ② divide — 주어 different languages(복수)에 맞는 동사원형 divide 맞아요.

❌ ④ recognizes — 주어 Adolphs(단수)에 맞는 단수동사 recognizes 맞아요.
det.tip: 명사 + 과거분사(identified): 확인'되는' 범주 (수동)
